shared_elements: horned animal head with spiral/curled horn
textured fleece rendered as rows of small incised scales/tufts
human figure associated with the animal (touching/holding it)
patterned coiffure or headgear rendered as a grid of small incised units
large staring eye with raised rim
justification: Both depict a horned animal with a tightly curled spiral horn beside a fleece rendered as regular rows of small incised scale-like tufts, and in both a human figure with a densely patterned coiffure/cap is directly attached to the animal, touching or holding it — a fairly specific man-and-ram combination with matching infill conventions for fleece and hair. The biggest difference in content is the composition: A is a lateral procession of two paired men and two rams in strict profile along a ground line, whereas B is a single compact figure-and-animal group conceived in the round with the animal held against the body, so the ordering and placement of elements do not correspond.
